title: SEIZURES, EARLY-ONSET, WITH NEURODEGENERATION AND BRAIN CALCIFICATIONS

relationships.phenotype: SEIZURES, EARLY-ONSET, WITH NEURODEGENERATION AND BRAIN CALCIFICATIONS

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that early-onset seizures with neurodegeneration and brain calcifications (SENEBAC) is caused by homozygous mutation in the NRROS gene (615322) on chromosome 3q29.

checks.claim: Early-onset seizures with neurodegeneration and brain calcifications (SENEBAC) is caused by homozygous mutation in the NRROS gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Exome sequencing identified homozygous NRROS variants in the affected children from both families
checks.explanation: The paper describes early-onset refractory seizures, neurodegeneration and calcification caused by homozygous NRROS variants.

checks.claim: The NRROS gene is located on chromosome 3q29.
checks.evidence_quote: Here, we describe a novel early onset lethal encephalopathy due to mutations in the microglial-associated protein NRROS.
checks.explanation: The paper does not give the chromosomal location, but under the instructions a gene's standard location counts as supported nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: SENEBAC is an autosomal recessive neurodegenerative disorder caused by biallelic mutations in NRROS (Smith et al., 2020). Seizures begin within the first year of life (Dong et al., 2020). Smith et al. (2020) reported normal early development, followed by refractory seizures and neurodegeneration. Brain imaging shows intracranial calcification and, later, white matter signal changes. The disease is progressive and led to death in early childhood. Smith et al. (2020) called the disorder a microgliopathy and suggested that NRROS functions in TGF-beta and reactive oxygen species regulation may be important in its pathogenesis.

checks.claim: SENEBAC is an autosomal recessive neurodegenerative disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: Exome sequencing identified homozygous NRROS variants in the affected children from both families
checks.explanation: The paper reports biallelic (homozygous) variants and neurodegeneration, which fits recessive inheritance. It never says 'autosomal recessive' in so many words.

checks.claim: SENEBAC is caused by biallelic mutations in NRROS.
checks.evidence_quote: Biallelic mutations in NRROS cause an early onset lethal microgliopathy.
checks.explanation: The paper's title states this directly.

checks.claim: In SENEBAC, seizures begin within the first year of life.
checks.evidence_quote: the onset of seizures occurred within the first year of life, followed by developmental regression
checks.explanation: The abstract states that seizures began within the first year of life.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2020) reported that patients with SENEBAC had normal early development.
checks.evidence_quote: All three children were born after a normal pregnancy and delivery, and early development was unremarkable.
checks.explanation: The paper states early development was unremarkable in all three children.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2020) reported that patients with SENEBAC developed refractory seizures after normal early development.
checks.evidence_quote: However, in the second year of life, they experienced the onset of refractory seizures and neurodegeneration
checks.explanation: Refractory seizures began in the second year, after unremarkable early development.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2020) reported that patients with SENEBAC developed neurodegeneration.
checks.evidence_quote: However, in the second year of life, they experienced the onset of refractory seizures and neurodegeneration
checks.explanation: The paper reports onset of neurodegeneration in all three children.

checks.claim: Brain imaging in SENEBAC shows intracranial calcification.
checks.evidence_quote: Neuroimaging initially demonstrated fine calcification at the depths of the cerebral gyri, with normal white matter
checks.explanation: Initial imaging showed calcification.

checks.claim: Later brain imaging in SENEBAC shows white matter signal changes.
checks.evidence_quote: As disease progressed, repeat imaging revealed increased calcification, severe generalized atrophy with ventricular dilatation, and diffuse signal changes in cerebral and cerebellar white matter.
checks.explanation: Repeat imaging later in the disease showed white matter signal changes.

checks.claim: SENEBAC is progressive.
checks.evidence_quote: As disease progressed, repeat imaging revealed increased calcification, severe generalized atrophy
checks.explanation: The paper describes a progressive course.

checks.claim: SENEBAC led to death in early childhood.
checks.evidence_quote: leading to death between the ages of 27 and 36 months
checks.explanation: Death occurred at 27 to 36 months, i.e. in early childhood.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2020) called SENEBAC a microgliopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: thereby suggesting a loss of NRROS function as a novel microgliopathy in humans
checks.explanation: The authors call the disorder a microgliopathy.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2020) suggested that NRROS functions in TGF-beta regulation and reactive oxygen species regulation may be important in the pathogenesis of SENEBAC.
checks.evidence_quote: Functions of NRROS proposed above, notably in ROS and TGFβ regulation, may be important in disease pathogenesis.
checks.explanation: The paper makes this suggestion directly.

paragraphs.text: Smith et al. (2020) reported affected children from 2 unrelated families. Neuroimaging showed calcification. Later imaging showed diffuse signal changes in the cerebral and cerebellar white matter. Follow-up showed rapidly progressive cortical and subcortical atrophy, and the patients died between 27 and 36 months of age. On neuropathologic examination, P2Y12 staining was lost and TMEM119 immunoreactivity was weak, indicating marked parenchymal microglial abnormalities. There was also widespread neuronal loss with reactive gliosis throughout the grey matter.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2020) reported affected children with SENEBAC from 2 unrelated families.
checks.evidence_quote: Patients 1 (P1) and P2, both females, were the first and third children of non-consanguineous parents of Maori descent (family F1442), whilst P3 (family F2382), a male, was the first child of first cousin south Asian parents
checks.explanation: The paper describes two separate families of different ancestry.

checks.claim: Neuroimaging in the SENEBAC patients reported by Smith et al. (2020) showed calcification.
checks.evidence_quote: Neuroimaging initially demonstrated fine calcification at the depths of the cerebral gyri, with normal white matter
checks.explanation: Neuroimaging showed calcification.

checks.claim: Later imaging in the SENEBAC patients reported by Smith et al. (2020) showed diffuse signal changes in the cerebral white matter and cerebellar white matter.
checks.evidence_quote: repeat imaging revealed increased calcification, severe generalized atrophy with ventricular dilatation, and diffuse signal changes in cerebral and cerebellar white matter
checks.explanation: Later imaging showed diffuse cerebral and cerebellar white matter signal changes.

checks.claim: Follow-up of the SENEBAC patients reported by Smith et al. (2020) showed rapidly progressive cortical and subcortical atrophy.
checks.evidence_quote: Follow-up shows rapidly progressive cortical and sub-cortical atrophy in P1 and P3.
checks.explanation: The rapidly progressive atrophy is described only for P1 and P3, not for all patients.

checks.claim: The SENEBAC patients reported by Smith et al. (2020) died between 27 and 36 months of age.
checks.evidence_quote: leading to death between the ages of 27 and 36 months
checks.explanation: The paper gives this exact age range for death.

checks.claim: On neuropathologic examination of the SENEBAC patients reported by Smith et al. (2020), P2Y12 staining was lost.
checks.evidence_quote: The present case showed disruption to the distribution, density, and cell morphology of IBA1 cells alongside loss of P2Y12 staining and weak TMEM119 immunoreactivity
checks.explanation: The neuropathology was done on only one patient (P3), not on the patients as a group.

checks.claim: On neuropathologic examination of the SENEBAC patients reported by Smith et al. (2020), TMEM119 immunoreactivity was weak.
checks.evidence_quote: The present case showed disruption to the distribution, density, and cell morphology of IBA1 cells alongside loss of P2Y12 staining and weak TMEM119 immunoreactivity
checks.explanation: The finding is correct but comes from a single case (P3), not all patients.

checks.claim: The loss of P2Y12 staining and weak TMEM119 immunoreactivity in the SENEBAC patients reported by Smith et al. (2020) indicated marked parenchymal microglial abnormalities.
checks.evidence_quote: alongside loss of P2Y12 staining and weak TMEM119 immunoreactivity, indicative of marked parenchymal microglial abnormalities
checks.explanation: The paper gives this interpretation, but it rests on only one examined case (P3).

checks.claim: Neuropathologic examination of the SENEBAC patients reported by Smith et al. (2020) showed widespread neuronal loss with reactive gliosis throughout the grey matter.
checks.evidence_quote: There was widespread neuronal loss with reactive gliosis throughout the grey matter (Supplementary Figure 3).
checks.explanation: The finding is correct, but pathology was done only on P3.

paragraphs.text: Dong et al. (2020) reported 6 individuals from 4 families with biallelic NRROS variants. Seizures began within the first year of life and were followed by developmental regression.

checks.claim: Dong et al. (2020) reported 6 individuals from 4 families with biallelic NRROS variants.
checks.evidence_quote: We report six individuals from four families with bi-allelic variants in NRROS.
checks.explanation: The patient and family counts match the abstract.

checks.claim: In the individuals with biallelic NRROS variants reported by Dong et al. (2020), seizures began within the first year of life.
checks.evidence_quote: the onset of seizures occurred within the first year of life
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: In the individuals with biallelic NRROS variants reported by Dong et al. (2020), seizure onset was followed by developmental regression.
checks.evidence_quote: the onset of seizures occurred within the first year of life, followed by developmental regression
checks.explanation: The abstract states that developmental regression followed seizure onset.

paragraphs.text: Smith et al. (2020) found homozygous NRROS mutations in the affected children from both families they studied. Biallelic mutations are consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2020) found homozygous NRROS mutations in the affected children from both families they studied.
checks.evidence_quote: Exome sequencing identified homozygous NRROS variants in the affected children from both families
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

checks.claim: Biallelic NRROS mutations in SENEBAC are consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: Biallelic mutations in NRROS cause an early onset lethal microgliopathy.
checks.explanation: The paper reports biallelic mutations (one family consanguineous) but never explicitly says the inheritance is autosomal recessive.

paragraphs.text: Smith et al. (2020) used exome sequencing to identify homozygous NRROS mutations in the affected children from 2 families. Both mutations were predicted to truncate the protein.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2020) used exome sequencing to identify homozygous NRROS mutations in the affected children from 2 families with SENEBAC.
checks.evidence_quote: Exome sequencing identified homozygous NRROS variants in the affected children from both families: a c.1777C > T/p.(Gln593*) and a c.1257del/p.(Gly420AlafsTer14) in F1442 and F2382, respectively.
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

checks.claim: Both NRROS mutations identified by Smith et al. (2020) were predicted to truncate the NRROS protein.
checks.evidence_quote: both of these variants are predicted to result in a truncated protein
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Dong et al. (2020) identified biallelic loss-of-function NRROS variants in affected individuals. These variants resulted in aberrant NRROS proteins with an impaired ability to anchor latent TGF-beta-1 on the cell surface. Dong et al. (2020) noted that this anchoring is required for activation of TGF-beta-1 in macrophages and microglia.

checks.claim: Dong et al. (2020) identified biallelic loss-of-function NRROS variants in individuals affected with SENEBAC.
checks.evidence_quote: Bi-allelic LoF NRROS Variants Impairing Active TGF-β1 Delivery Cause a Severe Infantile-Onset Neurodegenerative Condition
checks.explanation: The title describes the variants as biallelic loss-of-function. The name SENEBAC is not used in the paper, but the condition described is the same.

checks.claim: The NRROS variants identified by Dong et al. (2020) resulted in aberrant NRROS proteins.
checks.evidence_quote: These variants result in aberrant NRROS proteins with impaired ability to anchor latent TGF-β1 on the cell surface.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that the variants produce aberrant NRROS proteins.

checks.claim: The aberrant NRROS proteins resulting from the variants identified by Dong et al. (2020) had an impaired ability to anchor latent TGF-beta-1 on the cell surface.
checks.evidence_quote: These variants result in aberrant NRROS proteins with impaired ability to anchor latent TGF-β1 on the cell surface.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Dong et al. (2020) noted that NRROS anchoring of latent TGF-beta-1 on the cell surface is required for activation of TGF-beta-1 in macrophages and microglia.
checks.evidence_quote: anchors it on the cell surface; this anchoring is required for activation of TGF-β1 in macrophages and microglia
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Smith et al. (2020) noted that Nrros -/- mice lost the homeostatic microglial gene expression profile, including suppression of P2ry12 and Tmem119 expression. The mice developed progressive neurologic decline, and their neuropathology included neuronal loss.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2020) noted that Nrros -/- mice lost the homeostatic microglial gene expression profile.
checks.evidence_quote: Both Nrros−/− mouse studies observed a loss of homeostatic gene expression profile which included suppression of P2ry12 and Tmem119 expression
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2020) noted that Nrros -/- mice showed suppressed P2ry12 and Tmem119 expression.
checks.evidence_quote: Both Nrros−/− mouse studies observed a loss of homeostatic gene expression profile which included suppression of P2ry12 and Tmem119 expression
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2020) noted that Nrros -/- mice developed progressive neurologic decline.
checks.evidence_quote: Nrros−/−mice exhibited progressive neurological decline, including motor defects and abnormal locomotor activity, from age 2–3 months and death by 6 months of age.
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2020) noted that the neuropathology of Nrros -/- mice included neuronal loss.
checks.evidence_quote: Neuropathology in these mouse models includes neuronal loss, demyelination, axonal pathology, astrogliosis, and the increased presence of foamy macrophages
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.
